key_insight: Reusable, architecture-matched calibration can recover noise-suppressed quantum features and improve quantum neural network trainability without recalibrating at every training step.
engineering_relevance: Fixed feature estimators offer a practical way to improve noise-limited quantum learning while avoiding repeated calibration during optimization.
method: Calibrate a reference circuit with the same gate architecture as the trainable circuit.
Construct regularized estimators of local quantum features and keep them fixed throughout training.
Quantify how calibration errors and response mismatches affect recovered observables and derivatives.
evidence_signal: Simulations showed improved landscape contrast, convergence, and classification; an IBM Quantum experiment improved closed-loop optimization, and a modular demonstration reused calibration across 25 independent four-qubit channels.
watch_item: Calibration accuracy and noise-response matching remain critical; the 100-qubit aggregate demonstration comprises independent four-qubit channels, not one fully coupled 100-qubit QNN.
paper_title: Restoring quantum neural network trainability through reusable calibration
